blocks.why: Normal night at home before the month starts — you want to go into the ORD trip with a full tank.
Two hours in the early afternoon before you leave at 15:35 local, because this duty doesn't finish until 04:00 body time.
Straight down at the hotel after check-in — it's 04:40 body time and you'll drop instantly.
Early-afternoon top-up in Chicago so you can hold out for a late bedtime and start sliding towards the night return.
Deliberately late — 01:00 to 09:00 Chicago — so the anchor sleep sits as close as it can to the flight home.
Two hours late afternoon local, finishing well clear of the 19:40 pickup, to cover the whole eastbound night.
Home mid-afternoon after an all-night sector — take the edge off but stop by 19:00 local so you can still sleep tonight.
Full night in your own bed, waking just in time for the 07:45Z door for the JFK report.
Bed at 18:00 New York feels odd but it's midnight body time — stay on Madrid hours, you're only here two nights.
Short afternoon nap on the day off so you can push bedtime later tonight without wrecking yourself.
22:00–06:00 New York — the delayed anchor sleep that has to carry you through the 23:10 departure.
Two hours at 17:00–19:00 local, done two hours before the pickup, so you board with fresh legs for the overnight.
Post-night-flight recovery at home, capped at three hours so tonight still works.
First proper night back on Madrid time — this is the one that clears the ORD/JFK debt.
Day off, standard night — keep the rhythm regular through the break.
Last full night before the 14h53 quad-sector — protect it, you won't get another one for a day and a half.
Two hours at 11:00–13:00 local, an hour clear of leaving home, because you're going to be flying through 03:00–06:00 body time tonight.
Blackout blinds, straight to bed at 08:00 local after landing at 05:48 — this is the real recovery sleep.
Back onto a normal night the same day, so the body clock resets rather than drifting.
Day off, normal night.
Day off, normal night.
Day off, normal night.
Day off, normal night.
Start walking bedtime back by 90 minutes — the 05:05 report on the 19th needs a two-night run-up, not a one-night heroic.
Bank 90 minutes in the early afternoon, because you will not get a full night in front of an 05:05 sign-on.
Lights out at 20:00 local for a 03:00 alarm — it's an awkward hour to fall asleep, which is exactly why the afternoon nap is there.
Home from four sectors on an early — 90 minutes, finished by 19:30 local so it doesn't eat tonight.
Full night before an easy afternoon two-sector day — pull the clock straight back to normal.
Seven hours, waking a little early, to begin the slide towards Tuesday's 05:40 report.
Afternoon nap on the day off to make tonight's short, early night survivable.
Bed at 20:45 local for a 03:35 alarm — six hours fifty, the most this report time allows.
Two hours as soon as you get in, because tomorrow is an even earlier report and you need the credit now.
Early to bed at 20:00 local for the 04:35 report — second early in a row, so keep the evening dark and quiet.
Three hours off the back of two consecutive earlies — the next duty isn't until tomorrow lunchtime, so you can afford a long one.
Long night back on normal hours, front-loading sleep before a 12-hour four-sector day that lands at 23:44.
In the door at 01:39 local, wind down, and sleep through the morning — nothing on the 25th.
Clean full night before the Singapore sector — you'll be awake to 02:40 body time on arrival, so this is the whole reserve.
Into the hotel at 09:20 Singapore, straight to bed — it's 03:30 body time and the room is the right side of the day.
02:00–09:35 Singapore, which is still your Madrid night — one night here, so don't try to flip.
Home at 22:05 local after a 15h30 westbound — nine hours, no alarm, this is the reset.
Day off, normal night — second recovery night after Singapore.
Last night of the period, back on base time and clear for whatever October brings.

conflicts.statement: The MAD-DUB-MAD-FCO-MAD quad is rostered at 14h53, which is 1h53 over the 13-hour planning ceiling in FCM §4.1.3, and it runs straight through 03:00-06:00 body time on the last two sectors.
options: Query crewing before the day: this is a planning limit, so it should be fixed on the roster rather than discovered on the day.
Ask whether the FCO rotation (CR866/CR563) can be split off to another crew, which brings the duty back to about 7h20.
If it stands, use the 09:00-11:00Z pre-duty nap as non-negotiable and protect 12/09 morning at home completely — no errands, no phone.

conflicts.statement: MAD-SIN is rostered at 15h30 duty on 13h30 block, 2h30 over the FCM §4.1.3 ceiling. The roster also shows your rank as CP/A320, which does not sit with a 13h30 sector — one of the two is wrong.
options: Confirm with crewing whether this is an augmented/heavy crew operation with in-flight rest facilities, which is what a 15h30 FDP would need.
Confirm the aircraft type and your qualification on it before the day — if the type is wrong, the whole pairing may be misassigned.
If it is augmented, ask which rest slot you have; that changes whether you want the second or third break, and I can rework 26-27/09 around it.

conflicts.statement: SIN-MAD is the same shape in reverse — 15h30 duty, 13h30 block, 2h30 over the §4.1.3 ceiling, reporting at 11:10 Singapore which is 05:10 body time.
options: Raise it with the SIN pairing as one item rather than two, since the same answer covers both legs.
If augmented, take the earliest available bunk slot on this one — you'll have been awake since 09:35 local with a short night behind you.
Block out the evening of 28/09 and all of 29/09 at home; the nine-hour night I've planned is the minimum after a duty this shape.

conflicts.statement: In the 24 hours ending when you're released at MAD, the plan only gets you about 3h40 of sleep (the 21:30-23:30Z nap plus the tail of the Chicago anchor sleep). The eastbound night return doesn't leave room for more.
options: Accept the shortfall and take the 2h30 recovery nap at home on the 4th as planned — it's what makes the following night work.
Push the Chicago anchor sleep later still (08:00-16:00Z) if you can hold out that long on the 2nd; it moves roughly 2h of sleep into the deficit window.
Arrange not to drive yourself home from MAD on the 4th.

conflicts.statement: The JFK-MAD overnight leaves you about 2h of sleep in the 24 hours before release at 13:40 local — only the pre-duty nap falls inside that window.
options: Treat the 21:00-23:00Z nap at JFK as mandatory rather than optional; without it this duty has no sleep in it at all.
Shift the JFK anchor sleep on the 7th later (04:00-12:00Z) to pull more of it into the window, at the cost of a harder wake-up.
Don't drive from MAD on the 8th, and take the 3h recovery nap before doing anything else.

conflicts.statement: The 14h53 quad gives you roughly 3h40 in the 24 hours to release at 06:18 local, with the FCO sectors sitting squarely in the 02:00-06:00 body-clock trough.
options: This one follows directly from the duty-length problem — if the FDP gets shortened, the sleep shortfall goes with it.
If it stands, extend the pre-duty nap window on the 11th by going to bed earlier on the 10th, and take the full two hours.
Arrange a lift or a taxi home on the morning of the 12th; 06:18 release after an all-nighter is the worst drive of the month.

conflicts.statement: With a 09:10Z report there's no room for a pre-duty nap, so the 24 hours ending at your Singapore release only contain about 4h50 of sleep across a 15h30 duty.
options: If the flight is augmented, in-flight bunk rest closes most of this gap — confirm the rest plan and I'll re-cut the blocks around it.
Alternatively go to bed at 20:30Z on the 25th and wake at 03:30Z, which moves about an hour into the window but costs you an early start on a day off.
Protect the arrival sleep at SIN (01:30-08:30Z) absolutely — no crew dinner, no daylight before you've had seven hours.

conflicts.statement: An 05:05 report means leaving home at 03:40 local, so the most I can plan is 7h ending at 03:00 — and a 20:00 local bedtime is in the hardest part of the day to fall asleep, so realistic sleep is likely under that.
options: Take the 90-minute nap on the afternoon of the 18th; with it you're at 8h30 across the day even if the night runs short.
Move bedtime on the 17th earlier as planned so the 18th isn't a single big jump.
If you'd rather not have the split, say so and I'll plan one 7h block and drop the nap — but you'll be short on the day.
